Title: Prefix-matching Path Traversal in generateManifestGeneric
Analysis:
The `generateManifestGeneric` function in `cmpserver/plugin/plugin.go` computes an absolute `appPath` using `filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(workDir, metadata.AppRelPath))` and validates that it remains inside `workDir` using:
`!strings.HasPrefix(appPath, workDir)`

However, because `workDir` is not ensured to have a trailing path separator before checking prefix matching, it is vulnerable to a prefix mismatch bypass. For example, if `workDir` is `/tmp/cmp-work/1234abcd` and `metadata.AppRelPath` is `../1234abcd-other`, the resulting `appPath` evaluates to `/tmp/cmp-work/1234abcd-other`. The prefix check `strings.HasPrefix("/tmp/cmp-work/1234abcd-other", "/tmp/cmp-work/1234abcd")` returns `true`, allowing `appPath` to point to a directory outside `workDir`.

This directory is eventually passed to `s.generateManifest` and used as the working directory (`cmd.Dir`) for running commands configured in the plugin spec, which can execute files or locate configurations outside the expected temporary directory boundaries.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A malicious or compromised client sending metadata with:
```json
{
  "appRelPath": "../1234abcd-other"
}
```
will bypass the check and cause commands to execute within a sibling directory of the workdir.

Title: Prefix-matching Path Traversal in RelativePath
Analysis:
The `RelativePath` function in `util/io/files/util.go` cleans and validates if `fullPath` has a prefix of `basePath` by performing `strings.HasPrefix(fp, filepath.Clean(basePath))`. Because it does not append the path separator to the end of `basePath` before checking, it has a prefix mismatch vulnerability.

If `basePath` is `/tmp/_argocd-repo/12345` and `fullPath` is `/tmp/_argocd-repo/12345-other/somefile`, the `HasPrefix` check returns `true`, and `filepath.Rel` returns `../12345-other/somefile`, bypassing the intended boundary restriction.

This function is used during manifest compression in `GetCompressedRepoAndMetadata` in `util/cmp/stream.go` to construct `appRelPath`, which gets sent as `metadata.AppRelPath` to the CMP server. On the receiving side, the CMP server validates `AppRelPath` using the same flawed prefix check (without path separator), enabling execution directory traversal.

Title: Prefix-matching Path Traversal in argopath.Path
Analysis:
The `Path` function in `util/app/path/path.go` validates that a computed application path (`appPath`) resides inside a specified root directory (`root`) using `strings.HasPrefix(appPath, filepath.Clean(root))`. However, because `filepath.Clean(root)` does not ensure a trailing path separator (e.g. `/` or `\\`), the prefix check is vulnerable to a sibling directory prefix bypass.

For example, if `root` is `/tmp/_argocd-repo/12345` (representing the clone directory of a repository) and `path` is specified as `../12345-other`, the resulting `appPath` after joining and cleaning is `/tmp/_argocd-repo/12345-other`.
The validation checks `strings.HasPrefix("/tmp/_argocd-repo/12345-other", "/tmp/_argocd-repo/12345")`, which evaluates to `true` even though `/tmp/_argocd-repo/12345-other` resides completely outside the intended root directory.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
In an Application manifest, an attacker can specify `spec.source.path` as:
```yaml
spec:
  source:
    path: "../12345-other"
```
If a sibling repository cloned under `12345-other` exists in the `repo-server`'s temporary storage, the attacker is able to bypass boundaries and access the manifests of that sibling repository, potentially resulting in unauthorized information disclosure or logic manipulation.
